text: As the only night-shift supervisor at the Riverside warehouse, I never get a proper break.
I am the one who raised the forklift incident last month and nothing has changed.
Being the sole wheelchair user in the Downtown store, the staff room is impossible for me.
I joined the design desk at Northgate three weeks ago and have had no training.
Since I came back from maternity leave in June my hours in visual merchandising were cut.
As the longest-serving member of the returns team, twenty-two years, I think we deserve better.
I am the only French speaker in customer care so every French call lands on me.
After my transfer from Leeds to the Downtown finance team I feel left out.
Darren in dispatch shouts at the temps and nobody stops him.
The Northgate store manager plays favourites with the rota.
Priya Shah deserves a promotion, she carries the whole team.
My line manager, the head of visual merchandising, takes credit for our work.
The new HR business partner for Riverside ignores every email.
Tom from IT fixed my laptop in ten minutes, give him a raise.
Our regional director made a sexist joke at the town hall.
The Saturday shift lead on tills at Downtown lets her friends leave early.
We need more staff on weekends.
Pay has not kept up with the cost of living.
The break room microwave has been broken for ages.
Managers should communicate rota changes earlier.
I enjoy working here, the team is supportive.
Training on the new till system was rushed.
Some supervisors could listen more.
More flexible hours would help those of us with kids.
